result.title: Tokenization and Architecture Jointly Allocate Component Roles in Time Series Transformers
result.comment: Accepted at NeurIPS 2026. 42 pages, 3 figures. Code: https://github.com/mingyu-11/tokenization-component-roles
result.summary: Time series transformers have achieved strong forecasting performance, yet it remains unclear which of their components, attention or the feed-forward network (FFN), constructs temporal features, and how tokenization such as patching changes this. We propose a temporal probing framework that uses 15 token-level diagnostic tasks to measure feature construction as the gain in linear decodability of temporal properties from one sub-layer to the next (a matched MLP probe already saturates at the embedding). It targets models whose probed representations are read by a linear forecasting head. Applied to 5 supervised models trained on 8 long-term forecasting benchmarks, it finds that the constructing component is not fixed but allocated by the interaction of tokenization and architecture. Under patch tokenization (PatchTST), the FFN's gain exceeds attention's in probing on all 8 datasets, and its 8-dataset mean is 3.2x attention's. Without attention, the FFN alone reaches nearly the same total gain, both when attention is removed from a trained model and when PatchTST is trained without it, and the retrained model forecasts within a few percent of the full model. In probing, attention dominates under variate tokenization (iTransformer); in CATS, cross-attention is the only input path. In a controlled manipulation of PatchTST, single-scalar tokens (P=1) nearly eliminate the FFN's construction, while one more point per token (P=2) restores it. Our forecasting-side interventions (activation patching, knockout, and training without attention) establish component-level reliance and sufficiency. These results offer a representational reading of prior findings on the gains from patching, the competitiveness of self-attention-free models (TSMixer, PatchMLP), and the distinct role of cross-attention in CATS.

AI.brief_summary: 该论文提出时间序列 Transformer 的时间探测框架，用 15 个 token 级诊断任务、以子层间线性可解码性增益衡量 attention 与 FFN 各自构造了哪些时间特征，并结合 patch/变量 tokenization 对比、激活替换、knockout 与去 attention 重训进行验证，结论是组件角色由 tokenization 与架构共同分配。
AI.relevance_reason: 其「逐子层可解码性增益 + activation patching/knockout」的组件归因流程，可能可供核查 LVR 中 latent 表示由哪一模块构造、以及答案是否真正依赖这些表示；但属时间序列领域，迁移到视觉推理需较多判断。
